summary: Sanibel Island Light, Lee County, Florida: an iron skeleton tower lit in August 1884 at the island's eastern tip; its keepers' houses were lost to Hurricane Ian in 2022.

lens.where: Third-order lens removed in 1962; a 300 mm drum lens from a lightship replaced it (LighthouseFriends). The 300 mm lens is on display at the Sanibel Historical Museum (LighthouseFriends).

structures.note: Two frame dwellings on iron columns; swept away by Hurricane Ian in 2022 (LighthouseFriends; Florida Lighthouse Association).

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed to visitors. Reached from the eastern end of the island, where metered parking is signed.

facts.agency: City of Sanibel (owns and manages the lighthouse, per LighthouseFriends and the Florida Lighthouse Association); the U.S. Coast Guard maintains the active aid.

notes_for_editor: CHECKED 2026-10-22 (fact-check). Reservation order date: the NRHP page 5 image (text layer reads '18^3') shows 'December 19, 18' with a pen stroke over the third digit and a '3' after it; read as 1883, so the nomination's date and its Garfield signer are inconsistent, as the story says. First-light year: the City of Sanibel's 2023 statement (city manager at the relighting ceremony) gives 1885; the nomination (20 August 1884), LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record give 1884. The story reports both. Erosion hurricane: LighthouseFriends dates a storm erosion to 1947 (the year after England's 1946 arrival); the Florida Lighthouse Association dates a hurricane's erosion to 1891. The Board's FY-1892 entry 731 mentions only repairs, so 1891 is not repeated. No 1947 newspaper search was run. Money: LighthouseFriends says all $50,000 came in 1883; the nomination's second appropriation is 7 August 1882. Both reported. Causeway: LighthouseFriends' introduction gives 1963 for the causeway; its electrification paragraph gives 1962 for the causeway's completion. Both reported. Barry's killing (22 June 1919, a Sunday): the Herald (26 June 1919, p. 5) says 'Sunday evening'; LighthouseFriends, citing the Fort Meyers Press of 23 June, says about noon on the day before. Fort Myers Press not read directly. The Herald's text is OCR; 'Port Myers' is its spelling. Board citations: entry 731 is in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1892 (title page of the volume's second report, read in the corpus text); entry 761 is in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1894 (title page confirmed). Scan pages were not checked against printed pages (printed pp. unconfirmed). Keepers: the roster matched by name and position (0.09 km); the roster lines were copied from roster.py output. The stray 'assistant' 1919 line for Richard T. Barry was removed because the roster already has him as first assistant 1917 to 1919 (the old note wrongly said he was not on the roster). Living persons: refuge staff and later residents on LighthouseFriends (from 1949 onward) are omitted; keeper lines stop at the 1949 end of resident keeping. Atmosphere sources: NRHP's description of the 1884 dwellings; LighthouseFriends' family details (the pet deer). Clarence Rutland's 1930s stint (LighthouseFriends) has no roster line, so none was added. The 2000 BLM transfer and 2004 application (LighthouseFriends) are not in the story. The 1stFlorida and WINK search results were not read.
